strengths: UniAP addresses a useful training-systems problem with direct computer-vision relevance through ViT-Huge and Swin-Huge. Jointly selecting pipeline partitions and per-layer DP, TP, and FSDP configurations could reduce manual tuning and improve resource utilization.

Table 1 reports meaningful measured gains. On ENVB-8, ViT achieves 45.58 samples/s versus 38.74 for Alpa and 32.20 for Galvatron; Swin achieves 19.08 versus 13.90 for Galvatron. The 3.80× Llama-7B throughput improvement and faster searches when throughput ties also have practical value.

Evaluation spans five model families and four hardware environments, with weak-scaling results up to 64 DCUs. Appendix F reports 3.59% average throughput-estimation error on selected strategies, providing some support for the cost model.
The workflow diagrams, model specifications, solver settings, and topology-aware BERT case study make the system reasonably understandable and provide useful implementation context.
weaknesses: A consequential correctness gap in the central formulation drives my weak-reject recommendation. Equations (6a–c) enforce contiguity but not pipeline-stage order: for an edge u→v, assigning u to stage 2 and v to stage 1 satisfies these constraints and Eq. (7), while Eq. (4) charges zero cross-stage communication. The objective can therefore favor an artificially cheap assignment. Appendix B proves contiguity alone and does not resolve this discrepancy.

Memory feasibility is insufficiently supported. Algorithm 1 passes micro-batch size b=B/c to CostModeling, while Section 3.2 scales activation memory by batch size. Neither that description nor Eq. (5) explains how activations retained across all c micro-batches in GPipe without checkpointing are counted. This matters for strategy feasibility and the claimed OOM guarantee; no peak-memory validation is reported.

The optimality and complexity claims exceed the evidence. Appendix E permits a 60-second timeout and early termination after 15 seconds with an optimality gap below 4%, but achieved gaps are not reported. Treating solver runtime as constant in Section 3.5 bounds a time-budgeted search, not the complexity of obtaining an optimal solution. Low prediction error on selected strategies also does not establish optimality for actual throughput.

The experiments do not isolate the central contribution of joint optimization over hierarchical optimization. Figure 6 compares against inter-layer-only and intra-layer-only variants, establishing the benefit of combining parallelism types. It does not establish the advantage of joint search over a hierarchical planner using the same strategy space, cost model, and execution backend. Hierarchical decomposition alone does not imply suboptimality, and the reported difference in cost-model accuracy provides another possible explanation for the gains.

The solver-ready formulation is missing. The resharding terms in Eqs. (3) and (4) contain degree-four products of placement and strategy-selection variables, yet no auxiliary-variable reformulation into MIQP is supplied. This is potentially correctable, but it is an important reproducibility gap for a paper whose principal contribution is the optimization formulation.

Search-time improvements have a narrower interpretation than the broader efficiency argument suggests. The timing measures UOP and excludes profiling, while Section 4.2 attributes substantial gains to multithreaded Gurobi versus single-threaded baselines. These are useful implementation-level measurements, but total planning overhead and algorithmic efficiency under comparable CPU resources remain unquantified.

strengths: UniAP addresses a useful training-systems problem: jointly choosing pipeline placement and per-layer DP, TP, and FSDP strategies. Its evaluation on ViT and Swin establishes direct relevance to computer vision.

Table 1 reports meaningful measured gains. On ENVB-8, ViT throughput increases from the best baseline's 38.74 to 45.58 samples/s, and Swin improves from 13.90 to 19.08. Llama-7B achieves a 3.80× improvement on ENVC. Matching existing throughput while reducing strategy-search time is also valuable.

The evaluation spans V100, TITAN Xp, A100, and Hygon hardware. UniAP matches the best searched Megatron configurations on ENVD-32 with substantially shorter search times, and Table 4 demonstrates promising weak scaling to 64 DCUs.

The manuscript provides useful pseudocode, model configurations, solver settings, and a concrete strategy visualization. Appendix F reports 3.59% average throughput-estimation error on selected configurations, while Appendix G explains how the chosen strategies exploit communication topology.
weaknesses: The stated constraints do not enforce pipeline execution order. Equations (6a–6c) guarantee contiguity within each stage, but allow a chain u→v to place u on stage 2 and v on stage 1. This assignment satisfies the placement constraints, yet Equation (4) assigns zero communication cost to that edge because it counts only transfers from stage j to j+1. This is a substantive correctness gap in the optimization objective; Appendix B's contiguity proof does not resolve it.

The advertised MIQP formulation is not quadratic as written. Equations (3) and (4) contain products P_ui P_vi S_uk S_vl, which are degree four. Auxiliary variables can produce a quadratic reformulation, but the required variables and linking constraints are absent. Consequently, the actual optimization problem supplied to Gurobi is not reproducible from the manuscript.

The GPipe memory accounting appears incomplete. Algorithm 1 passes micro-batch size b=B/c to cost modeling, Section 3.2 scales activation memory by that batch size, and Equation (5) introduces no factor accounting for retained activations across micro-batches. GPipe retains activations from all c forward micro-batches before backward execution. As specified, the constraint can underestimate peak memory. No peak-memory validation resolves this concern, and Figure 6 also reports an OOM outcome for an intra-layer-only ablation.

The repeated global-optimality claims exceed the evidence. Appendix E uses a 60-second solver limit and allows termination after 15 seconds with a gap below 4%, but achieved gaps and termination statuses are unreported. Optimality would additionally be relative to the approximate cost model and restricted candidate space. Section 3.5's complexity argument treats solver runtime as constant through a timeout; this does not establish the complexity of finding an exact optimum.

The experiments do not isolate the claimed advantage of joint optimization over hierarchical optimization. Figure 6 removes either inter-layer or intra-layer parallelism; it does not compare joint and hierarchical searches using the same strategies, cost model, and execution backend. Hierarchical optimization is not inherently suboptimal, so the categorical statements in Section 2 and Figure 1 need stronger justification.

Some validation and reproducibility limitations remain: Appendix F measures prediction error only for selected solutions, without testing candidate rankings; search-time comparisons partly reflect multithreaded Gurobi versus single-threaded baselines, without explicit thread budgets; and profiling overhead is excluded from the reported UOP time. These reservations alone would not determine rejection. My Weak Reject is driven primarily by the unresolved formulation and memory-feasibility issues, despite the worthwhile measured systems gains.

Equations (6a–c) enforce contiguity, not topological ordering of stage indices. For a chain u→v, placing u in stage 2 and v in stage 1 satisfies these and the placement constraints, but Equation (4) assigns their communication zero cost because it counts only edges from stage j to j+1. Memory feasibility is insufficiently justified for GPipe. Algorithm 1 passes micro-batch size b=B/c to CostModeling, while Section 3.2 scales activation memory by the supplied batch size. The formulation does not account explicitly for retaining activations from all c micro-batches before backward execution. With checkpointing disabled, this can substantially underestimate peak memory. Throughput-estimation accuracy does not validate this feasibility constraint.

The optimality claims exceed the evidence. Appendix E imposes a 60-second solver limit and permits stopping with a relative optimality gap below 4%, but achieved gaps are not reported. Even an exact solve would optimize an estimated objective within the enumerated candidate space. Section 3.5's runtime bound describes a time-capped procedure, not the complexity of obtaining the claimed optimum.

The ablation does not isolate the central contribution over hierarchical optimization. Figure 6 compares joint parallelism against inter-layer-only and intra-layer-only variants; existing hierarchical baselines already combine these categories. A comparison using the same candidate strategies, cost model, and execution backend is missing. Consequently, the results support combining parallelism types but do not establish that joint optimization itself causes the gains or that hierarchy inherently produces suboptimal solutions.

The connection between the equations and the implemented solver is incomplete. Equations (3) and (4) contain fourth-degree products of placement and strategy variables, rather than quadratic expressions. Standard auxiliary-variable reformulations could address this, but their linking constraints are not provided. The strategy dictionary and device-mapping rules also lack sufficient specification, and the manuscript supplies no UniAP implementation link. strengths: UniAP addresses a useful problem: jointly selecting pipeline placement and per-layer DP, TP, and FSDP strategies under communication and memory constraints. Its evaluation on ViT-Huge and Swin-Huge establishes direct relevance to large-scale visual learning.

The measured throughput improvements are meaningful. On ENVB-8, Table 1 reports ViT throughput of 45.58 samples/s versus 38.74 for Alpa and 32.20 for Galvatron, and Swin throughput of 19.08 versus 13.90 for Galvatron. The reported 3.80× Llama-7B improvement is also substantial.

Evaluation covers five Transformer families and four hardware environments, including non-NVIDIA accelerators. Table 4 supports near-linear weak scaling through 64 DCUs. Matching Galvatron's throughput while substantially reducing search time on several ENVA workloads also provides practical value.

The appendix supplies useful model configurations, solver settings, and an informative example of topology-aware strategy selection. The reported 3.59% average throughput-estimation error provides initial empirical support for the cost model.
weaknesses: The stated optimizer has a substantive correctness defect. Equation (6) enforces contiguity but does not enforce pipeline-stage ordering. For a two-layer chain u→v, assigning u to stage 2 and v to stage 1 satisfies the placement and contiguity constraints, yet Equation (4) assigns zero communication cost because it counts only edges from stage j to j+1. Consequently, the objective can prefer assignments that omit required transfers. Appendix B proves contiguity only and does not resolve this issue. This directly undermines the central formulation.

The advertised MIQP is incompletely specified: Equations (3) and (4) contain products of four binary variables, such as P_ui P_vi S_uk S_vl. These are quartic expressions. An auxiliary-variable reformulation is possible, but the manuscript does not provide the reduction and linking constraints used by Gurobi. This is an important reproducibility gap, although the missing reduction alone would be readily correctable.

The repeated optimality claims exceed the evidence. Appendix E specifies a 60-second solver limit and early termination with a relative optimality gap below 4%, but reports neither achieved gaps nor the proportion of instances solved to optimality. Section 3.5's fixed-deadline argument cannot establish polynomial-time optimal optimization. Furthermore, solver guarantees would concern the approximate cost model and restricted candidate space; measured throughput optimality is not established.

Memory feasibility needs stronger justification. Algorithm 1 passes micro-batch size b=B/c into cost modeling, while Section 3.2 describes activation memory as proportional to batch size without explaining accumulation across the micro-batches retained by GPipe. Figure 6 reports a CUDA OOM for an optimizer-selected intra-layer-only configuration, demonstrating that the stated memory guarantee can fail. Appendix F evaluates throughput prediction but supplies no corresponding memory validation.

The ablation does not isolate the main claimed methodological advantage. Figure 6 compares joint parallelism against inter-layer-only and intra-layer-only variants, establishing the value of combining parallel modes. It does not establish an advantage over hierarchical optimization with comparable candidate strategies, cost estimates, and execution infrastructure. Hierarchical decomposition itself does not necessarily imply suboptimality; restrictions in the conditional searches must be identified.

The search-speedup interpretation requires qualification. Section 4.1 measures UniAP's UOP time, excluding profiling, and Section 4.2 attributes substantial gains to multithreaded Gurobi versus single-threaded baseline searches. Profiling costs and matched CPU-resource comparisons are absent, limiting conclusions about total setup savings and algorithmic efficiency. This admits spuriously cheap solutions and leaves the relationship between the formulation and the implemented experiments unresolved.

Terms such as P_ui P_vi (S_u^T R_uv S_v) in Equation (3), and corresponding terms in Equation (4), are fourth-degree expressions in the binary decision variables. Auxiliary-variable reformulations are possible, but none is specified. Since the mathematical formulation is a central contribution, the missing reduction materially limits verification and reproducibility.

The repeated optimality claims exceed the evidence. Appendix E allows 60-second timeouts and early termination with a relative optimality gap below 4%, but achieved gaps and termination statuses are not reported. Section 3.5 obtains its complexity bound by imposing a constant solver timeout; this bounds a capped search rather than establishing the complexity of obtaining an optimal solution. Optimality under the approximate cost model also does not establish optimal measured throughput.

Peak-memory feasibility is insufficiently established. Algorithm 1 constructs the memory model using micro-batch size B/c, while Equation (5) does not explicitly account for the c activation sets retained by GPipe before backward execution when checkpointing is disabled. As written, this can underestimate memory. No peak-memory validation resolves this issue, and Figure 6 also reports an OOM outcome for an intra-layer-only UniAP variant despite its memory constraint.

The ablation does not isolate the claimed advantage of joint optimization over hierarchical optimization. Figure 6 removes either inter-layer or intra-layer strategies, showing that combining both is useful. It does not compare joint and hierarchical planners using the same candidate strategies, cost model, and execution backend. Hierarchical decomposition alone does not imply suboptimality, so the paper’s broad explanation of its novelty and performance advantage remains insufficiently supported.

The optimization-time results have a narrower interpretation than the headline suggests. UniAP timing measures UOP and excludes profiling, while Section 4.2 attributes substantial gains to multithreaded Gurobi versus single-threaded baselines. Equations (6a–c) enforce contiguity but allow an edge u→v with u assigned to stage 2 and v to stage 1. Equation (4) then assigns zero communication cost to this required transfer because it counts only edges from stage j to j+1. Thus even a two-layer chain admits an artificially favorable objective. Appendix B proves contiguity only and does not resolve this problem. This materially weakens confidence that the formulation optimizes the intended training schedule.

Such terms can be reformulated using auxiliary variables, but the manuscript supplies neither that construction nor the resulting solver formulation. Although mathematically repairable, this omission prevents reproducing and verifying the central optimization method.

The repeated optimality claims exceed the evidence. Appendix E specifies a 60-second time limit and early termination below a 4% optimality gap, without reporting achieved gaps or termination statuses. Consequently, Section 3.5 bounds a time-capped search procedure, not the computation required to obtain an optimal solution. Any guarantee would also concern the restricted candidate space and estimated costs, rather than actual training throughput.

Memory feasibility is insufficiently specified. Algorithm 1 constructs the memory costs using micro-batch size b=B/c, while Equation (5) shows no accounting for activation accumulation across micro-batches. strengths: UniAP addresses a useful systems problem: selecting pipeline, data, tensor, and fully sharded data parallelism together under communication and memory constraints. Its evaluation on ViT and Swin establishes direct relevance to computer vision.

Table 1 reports meaningful measured gains. On ENVB-8, ViT-Huge reaches 45.58 samples/s versus 38.74 for Alpa and 32.20 for Galvatron; Swin-Huge improves from 13.90 to 19.08 samples/s. Llama-7B on ENVC improves from 1.22 to 4.63 samples/s over Galvatron.

The experiments cover five model families and four hardware environments. The DCU experiments demonstrate approximately linear weak scaling through 64 devices, and UniAP matches the best enumerated Megatron configurations while substantially reducing reported strategy-search time.

The workflow, hardware descriptions, model configurations, and solver settings provide useful implementation context. Appendix F reports a 3.59% average throughput-estimation error, versus 11.17% for Galvatron, while the BERT case study illustrates a plausible combination of all four parallelism types.
weaknesses: The written formulation has a consequential stage-ordering gap. Equations (6a–6c) enforce contiguity, but do not order pipeline stages. For an edge u→v, assigning u to stage 2 and v to stage 1 satisfies these constraints and Equation (7), yet Equation (4) assigns no communication cost because it counts only j→j+1 transfers. Thus even a two-layer chain admits incorrectly costed placements. Appendix B proves contiguity, not the ordering needed by the objective. This central correctness issue weighs heavily toward weak rejection despite the empirical merits.

The claimed MIQP is not actually specified in quadratic form: Equations (3–4) contain products P_ui P_vi S_uk S_vl, which are quartic in the decision variables. An exact reformulation using auxiliary variables is possible, but the required variables and linking constraints are absent. This is a substantive reproducibility gap between the mathematical presentation and the reported Gurobi implementation.

Peak activation memory is insufficiently explained for the adopted GPipe schedule. Algorithm 1 passes micro-batch size b=B/c to CostModeling, and Section 3.2 scales activation memory by the supplied batch size. Without checkpointing, GPipe retains activations from multiple micro-batches before backward execution; the formulation does not explain the necessary accumulation across c micro-batches. Consequently, Equation (5)'s claimed protection against OOM is not established by the described model.

The optimality and complexity claims exceed what is demonstrated. Appendix E imposes a 60-second solver limit and permits termination after 15 seconds with an optimality gap below 4%, but achieved gaps and termination statuses are not reported. Section 3.5's polynomial runtime expression concerns a time-capped search, not guaranteed exact optimization. Furthermore, optimality for an approximate cost model within the enumerated candidate space does not establish optimal measured throughput.

The experiments do not isolate the central advantage claimed for joint optimization over hierarchical optimization. Figure 6 removes either inter-layer or intra-layer parallelism entirely; existing hierarchical methods support both. A comparison using the same candidates, cost model, and execution backend is missing. Hierarchical decomposition does not inherently imply suboptimality, so the categorical novelty and search-space claims need stronger justification.

The search-time results have a narrower interpretation than the headline ratios suggest. Section 4.1 measures UniAP's UOP and excludes profiling, while corresponding baseline timing boundaries are insufficiently specified. Section 4.2 also attributes substantial acceleration to solver multithreading. These results support practical search-phase speedups, but do not establish how much improvement comes from the proposed formulation or quantify total setup cost.
